nodes.title: Walk
nodes.goal: Load the West Loop walk: one row, its video, read in place from the SideSeeing bucket.

nodes.content:
from sam3_tracking import track_objects

# The Widgets tab sets what to look for, in plain words (SAM 3 takes any short
# noun phrase), the gap between two frames SAM 3 looks at, where the part of
# each video to track starts, in seconds from its start, the most frames of a
# video one run looks at, and the widest frames are read and drawn at. These
# two may be None, which no widget holds, so they are set here:
FORGET_SECONDS = 10  # SAM 3 lets go of an object unseen this long; None keeps every object
TO_SECONDS = None  # where the part of each video ends; None is the video's end

return track_objects(
    input_0, curio_load_model("model.curio.sam3"), curio_derived_file,
    labels=[!! labels !!], every_seconds=float([!! every_seconds !!]), forget_seconds=FORGET_SECONDS,
    from_seconds=float([!! from_seconds !!]), to_seconds=TO_SECONDS,
    max_frames=int([!! max_frames !!]), width=int([!! width !!]),
)
nodes.goal: Look for nine kinds of sidewalk object through the whole walk with SAM 3, a frame every 2.5 s, and give back two tables: its overlay, and its tracks, one row per object it follows.
Play the overlay in its videos tab: the frames SAM 3 looked at, each object's mask and id drawn on them.

nodes.title: Objects
nodes.content:
# One row per object Track Objects followed: its tracks table, read by its
# key. t_s, the time the player's range is matched on, is when SAM 3 first
# saw the object, so its bar takes its label's color from there.
objects = [!! input_0:tracks !!]
objects["t_s"] = objects["start_s"]

return objects
nodes.goal: Take Track Objects' tracks, one row per object, with t_s, when SAM 3 first saw it.

nodes.title: Swimlane
nodes.goal: Draw each object as a bar from its first sighting to its last, in its label's lane: in its label's color once the video has played past its first sighting, gray before.

nodes.title: GPS fixes
nodes.goal: Load the listing of the walk's gps.csv, read in place from the SideSeeing bucket.

nodes.title: Walk track
nodes.content:
import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd

walk, gps = [!! input_0 !!], [!! input_1 !!]

# The walk's GPS fixes, read in place from the gps.csv the GPS track's row names.
path = gps["path"].iloc[0]
if not path:
    raise ValueError("gps.csv is not on this machine yet: cache the GPS track's files in the Data Catalog first")
fixes = pd.read_csv(path)

# t_s, each fix's time in the walk, in seconds, which the player's range is
# matched on: its datetime_utc less the walk's taken_at, both in UTC.
taken_at = pd.to_datetime(walk["taken_at"].iloc[0], utc=True)
fixes["t_s"] = (pd.to_datetime(fixes["datetime_utc"], utc=True) - taken_at).dt.total_seconds()

return gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    fixes, geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(fixes["longitude"], fixes["latitude"]), crs="EPSG:4326",
)
nodes.goal: Read the walk's GPS fixes in place, each a point with t_s, its time in the walk.

nodes.title: Map
nodes.goal: Map the fixes over the West Loop's streets, colored by their time in the walk, those up to where the video stands in Autark's highlight color instead.

dataflow.name: SideSeeing: objects tracked along a walk
dataflow.description: A SideSeeing walk along the sidewalks of Chicago's West Loop, its 14 minute video read in place from the SideSeeing bucket: SAM 3 looks for nine kinds of sidewalk object through it, a frame every 2.5 s, and Simple View plays the overlay it draws. As the video plays, each object's bar on a swimlane turns from gray to its label's color at its first sighting, and the walk's GPS fixes on an Autark map of its streets, up to where the video stands, take Autark's highlight color in place of their colors by time.
dataflow.task: Track sidewalk objects through a walk's video with SAM 3, and follow them on a timeline and a map as the video plays.
